newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU gives qualified blessing to Italian EMU plans.
newsitem.headline: EU gives qualified blessing to Italian EMU plans.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday gave a qualified thumbs up to Italy's plans for qualifying for the single currency, warning that further economic measures may be needed.
EU sources said the ministers meeting in Brussels had welcomed moves made by Italy to prepare for economic and monetary union (EMU), praising Rome for what had been done so far.
But the ministers also questioned whether enough had been done to meet the strict requirements for EMU laid out in the Maastricht treaty.
"There was encouragement on the one hand but also an invitation to be very tough," one diplomat said.
Another source quoted German Finance Minister Theo Waigel as saying: "Perhaps other measures will be needed for lasting and durable budget consolidation."

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn was quoted as saying that EU countries needed to take account of the difficult circumstances under which Italy had made budgetary reforms, but other efforts would have to be made.
Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told his fellow ministers that Italy was prepared to do what was necessary.
"If needed to respect the criteria, we will take other measures," he was quoted as saying.

The Italian blueprint for EMU foresees a budget deficit of 3.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product this year, in line with the criterion for EMU. It also projects that the ratio will drop to 2.8 percent in 1998.
In terms of growth, GDP is expected to advance by 1.2 percent this year and 2.0 percent in 1998.
EU sources said some ministers had queried the 1.2 percent projected, especially given the slack performance to date of the Italian economy.
Ciampi said his government stuck by the projection, sources said.
Diplomats said Italy was encouraged to rely more heavily on spending cuts rather tax increases as well as adopting further measures to reform pensions and social security.
